ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 05.11.2016 PASSED BY THE II ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS COURT AND ADDITIONAL MACT, BIDAR SITTING AT BASAVAKALYAN IN M.V.C.NO.738/2015 BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is by the claimant in MVC.No.738/2015 on the file of the II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bidar sitting at Basavakalyan, Dist: Bidar, (for short 'Tribunal') against judgment and award passed in the said case dated 05.11.2016, claiming for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bidar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 02. The parties will be referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for sake of convenience.
Brief facts of the case are that on 01.04.2014, the claimant was going on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 1725, as a pillion rider.
The rider of the said motorcycle rode the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result of which, the accident had take place.
Due to which, the claimant had sustained grievous head injury.
The claimant had taken the treatment in Government Hospital at Bidar.
She had spent huge amount towards the medical expenses.
She was aged about 40 years and working as coolie as well as Tailor and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, she is unable to do her regular work and lost her earnings.
With these reasons prayed to award the compensation.
04. The respondent No.2 - insurance company disputed the contents of the claim petition and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
05. From the rival contentions of both the parties, the Tribunal had framed the necessary issues for determination.

Vimalabai vs Santosh And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43045359/
2 NC: 2024:KHC-K:4942
06. The claimant examined PW.1 and PW.2 and got market Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19 and closed her evidence.
The respondents had not led any evidence.
07. The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence available on record held that the accident had taken place, due to negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.

The Tribunal assessed the age of the claimant as 40 years, income taken at Rs.6,000/- per month, disability considered at 10% to the whole body, applied multiplier at 15 and awarded the following amount of compensation and directed the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation.
Sl. Heads of Compensation Amount No. (in Rs.)

01. Pain and suffering 25,000/-
02. Loss of life amenities and 20,000/-
 pleasure 03.

Medical attendant charges, food 20,000/-
and nutrition charges and transportation charges 04. Loss of income during laid up 12,000/-
period (Rs.6,000/- x 2)

Medical Expenses 1,90,000/-
Total 3,75,000/-
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4942 08.
Heard the arguments.
09. The learned counsel for the claimant would submit that the Tribunal has not considered the income of the claimant properly.
The amount of compensation awarded under all the heads are on lower side.
Hence, prayed for enhancement of the compensation.
10. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - insurance company supported the impugned judgment and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

Vimalabai vs Santosh And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43045359/
3 11.
The fact of accident and involvement of the vehicle in the accident in not in dispute.
The claimant had sustained head injury.
She had admitted as inpatient in the Hospital for 09 to 10 days.
According to her evidence, she has been suffering from the weakness of the body and also suffering from continuous pain in the head, which is corroborated by PW.2, though he is not a neurologist.
PW.2 says that her hearing is impaired.
However, the wound certificate does not disclose the same.
There are no materials on record to show that she had consulted the ENT Specialist and got the treatment, therefore, it cannot be considered.
The income assessed by the Tribunal is on lower side.

If the chart prepared by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority is considered, then the income of the claimant could be taken at Rs.7,500/-
per month.
As rightly submitted by the learned counsel for the claimant, compensation awarded under other heads except medical expenses, are on lower side, which needs to be enhanced.

Accordingly, the following amount of compensation is awarded:-
Sl. Heads of Compensation Amount No. (in Rs.)

01. Pain and suffering 35,000/-
02. Loss of amenities 40,000/-
03.
Attendant charges, special diet 30,000/- and conveyance charges 04.

Medical expenses 1,90,000/-
05. Loss of income during laid up 22,500/- period 06.

Loss of future earning capacity 1,35,000/-
duty permanent disability (Rs.7,500/-x12x15x10/100) Total 4,52,500/-
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4942 13.
The claimant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.77,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the petition, till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation.

14. For the above said discussion, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Bidar sitting at Basavakalyan, Dist: Bidar, in MVC.No.738/2015 dated 05.11.2016 is modified; A)
